items.title: 1. Core Tree Architecture & Sizing
items.text:
Controls how deep and wide the tree can grow before termination.

Set the classification class count with GrowthControl(n_classes=...). Existing calls can supply n_classes as a flat constructor keyword, a fit keyword, or a legacy LeafControl setting.

Parameter Type Default Valid Range Description max_depth int 5 [1, 64] Maximum tree depth from root to any leaf. Set to 1 for decision stumps; increase to 8-12 to capture deep multi-way interactions. max_leaf_nodes int \| None None [2, \infty) Maximum number of terminal leaf nodes. If set, growth follows best-first priority queue until leaf limit is reached. min_rows int 50 [1, \infty) Minimum number of samples required to form a terminal leaf (minbucket in R / min_child_samples in LightGBM). Prevents overfitting to tiny sub-populations. minsplit int \| None None [2, \infty) Minimum number of samples required to attempt a split. If None, defaults to 2 * min_rows. minprob float 0.02 (0.0, 0.5) Minimum fraction of training rows required in a terminal node (\(N_{\text{leaf}} / N \ge \text{minprob}\)). Safeguards against isolated slivers. min_gain float 1e-9 [0.0, \infty) Minimum impurity reduction required to justify creating child nodes. Analogous to min_split_gain in LightGBM or gamma in XGBoost.

items.title: 2. Splitting & Search Space Controls
items.text:
Governs candidate generation, feature subsampling, and candidate evaluations.

Parameter Type Default Options Description gain str \| None None "entropy", "gini", "variance" Split evaluation objective. If None, automatically resolves to "entropy" for classification and "variance" for regression. split_eval str "fast" "fast", "exact" Split evaluation engine. "fast" utilizes SIMD vectorization and streaming histogram accumulators; "exact" re-evaluates all continuous thresholds without binning. split_precision int \| None 4 [1, 16] Decimal digit rounding applied to candidate thresholds. Rounds continuous splits (e.g. 3.1416 instead of 3.1415926535) to prevent floating-point overfitting and improve explainability. split_cols list[int] \| list[str] \| None None Feature subset Whitelist of features permitted to form splits. Useful when reserving specific features solely for leaf linear models. col_sample float \| None None (0.0, 1.0] Fraction of features randomly subsampled at each split decision (colsample_bytree in XGBoost / mtry ratio). Injects stochastic decorrelation across ensemble trees. col_weights list[float] \| None None Non-negative weights Prior weights determining the sampling probability of each feature during candidate selection. Higher weights bias search toward key business drivers. interaction_groups list[list[int \| str]] \| None None Feature sets Enforces interaction constraints: features may only appear on the same root-to-leaf path if they belong to a shared interaction group. Prevents disallowed cross-variable leakage. presort bool False True, False Whether to pre-sort continuous features at the root. Reduces per-node sort overhead at the cost of initial fit memory.

items.title: 3. Regularization, Purity Gates & Split Penalties
items.text:
Structural regularization mechanisms designed to suppress noisy split boundaries.

Parameter Type Default Valid Range Description purity_gate float \| None None (0.0, 1.0) Purity stopping criterion. If a node's target standard deviation or Gini impurity falls below this fraction of global variance, node splitting halts early. purity_gate_metric str "sd" "sd", "iqr", "mad" Metric for evaluating node purity: standard deviation ("sd"), interquartile range ("iqr"), or median absolute deviation ("mad"). tail_quantile float \| None None (0.0, 0.25) Extrema protection threshold. Penalizes splits that isolate extreme target quantiles into tiny leaves. imbalance_penalty float 0.0 [0.0, 1.0] Penalizes asymmetric splits where $ alpha float 0.0 [0.0, \infty) Structural complexity penalty subtracted from the candidate split gain (\(G' = G - \alpha\)). Forces simpler tree topologies.

items.title: 4. Statistical Hypothesis Stopping & Pre-Selection
items.text:
Replaces heuristic gain thresholds with formal statistical hypothesis testing (analogous to CHAID and partykit::ctree).

Parameter Type Default Options Description split_test str "none" "none", "f_test", "permutation" Formal statistical test evaluated on prospective splits. Halts recursion when null hypothesis of independence cannot be rejected. split_alpha float 0.05 (0.0, 1.0) Significance level threshold (\(p < \alpha\)) required to accept a split candidate. bonferroni bool False True, False Applies Bonferroni multiplicity correction (\(p < \alpha / P\)) adjusting for the number of tested feature candidates. Eliminates selection bias toward high-cardinality features. preselect str "none" "none", "variance", "correlation" Heuristic screening step executed before split scans to discard uninformative columns. min_relevance float \| None None [0.0, 1.0] Minimum correlation/mutual information required to include a feature in split search.

items.title: 5. Categorical Handling & Monotonicity Constraints
items.text:
Native handling of categorical variables and directional domain knowledge.

Parameter Type Default Options Description cat_order str \| None None "target", "frequency", "natural" Categorical level ordering strategy. "target" orders levels by target mean/rate, converting combinatorial \(2^{K-1}\) subset search into linear \(O(K)\) boundary scans (Fisher's exact theorem). cat_search str "cumulative" "cumulative", "exhaustive" Partition search algorithm across ordered levels. "cumulative" checks consecutive level subsets; "exhaustive" evaluates all partition subsets (small \(K\) only). monotone list[int] \| None None [-1, 0, +1] Monotonicity constraints per feature: +1 forces non-decreasing target response, -1 forces non-increasing, 0 unconstrained. tree_monotone list[int] \| None None [-1, 0, +1] Enforces monotonic split step direction across parent-child tree partitions. leaf_monotone list[int] \| None None [-1, 0, +1] Enforces non-negative/non-positive sign constraints on leaf GLM linear coefficients.

items.title: 6. Pruning, Honesty & Missing Value Routing
items.text:
Controls post-fit pruning, missing value handling, and sample splitting.

Parameter Type Default Options Description prune str "cp" "cp", "cost_complexity", "bic", "aic", "none" Post-pruning algorithm. "cp" matches CART/rpart complexity pruning; "bic" penalizes number of active parameters using Bayesian Information Criterion. cp_alpha float 5.0 [0.0, \infty) Complexity pruning penalty multiplier. Higher values produce shallower, more general trees. honesty bool False True, False Enables honest estimation (Wager & Athey 2018). Tree splits are learned on a training sub-sample, while leaf models are fitted on a held-out estimation sub-sample. Guarantees asymptotic normality. honesty_fraction float 0.5 (0.0, 1.0) Proportion of rows allocated to the split-learning sub-sample when honesty=True. maxsurrogate int 0 [0, 10] Number of surrogate split variables stored per node (CART style). When a primary split feature is missing during prediction, the highest-agreement surrogate variable routes the sample.

items.title: 7. Leaf Models, GLM Families & Penalized Solvers
items.text:
Defines the parametric or non-parametric local model fitted within each terminal leaf.

Parameter Type Default Options Description leaf str "linear" "linear", "mean", "median", "quantile", "huber", "mars", "knn" Mathematical formulation of the leaf model: piecewise linear OLS ("linear"), constant mean ("mean"), median ("median"), Huber robust regression ("huber"), adaptive splines ("mars"), or non-parametric nearest neighbors ("knn"). knn_k int 5 [1, \infty) Number of nearest neighbors queried at leaf inference time. knn_variant str "uniform" "uniform", "distance", "exponential", "dual", "double" Weighting scheme for leaf KNN: "uniform" (unweighted), "distance" (inverse distance \(1/(d+\epsilon)^p\)), "exponential" (\(\exp(-\gamma d)\)), "dual" (distance \(\times\) compactness), or "double" (DW-KNN: distance consistency \(\times\) neighbor reliability \(v_i\)). knn_metric str "euclidean" "euclidean", "manhattan", "chebyshev", "minkowski", "cosine", "correlation", "canberra", "braycurtis", "gower", "mahalanobis" Distance proximity metric across leaf feature coordinates. "gower" normalizes mixed continuous/categorical features and handles missing entries; "mahalanobis" applies diagonal variance scaling. knn_k_validity int 5 [1, \infty) Secondary neighborhood size for precomputing neighbor reliability \(v_i\) (DW-KNN) or local compactness during fit(). knn_gamma float \| None None (0.0, \infty) Exponential spatial decay rate parameter. If None, automatically calibrated by the inverse median neighbor distance within the queried leaf. knn_p float 2.0 (0.0, \infty) Power parameter \(p\) for Minkowski metric or inverse distance weighting (\(1 / (d + \epsilon)^p\)). leaf_family str "gaussian" "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "tweedie", "tobit", "softmax" Target distribution family for Generalized Linear Model (GLM) leaves. "gaussian" uses identity link, "binomial" uses logit link, "poisson" uses log link. leaf_solver str "irls" "irls", "lbfgs", "ccd", "cmaes", "shade", "nes", "ga" Local optimization solver for leaf regression models: Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares / exact normal Cholesky ("irls"), Quasi-Newton L-BFGS with Armijo line search ("lbfgs"), Cyclic Coordinate Descent with active set ("ccd"), or SOTA continuous evolutionary algorithms: Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy ("cmaes"), Success-History Adaptive Differential Evolution ("shade"), Separable Natural Evolution Strategies ("nes"), or Real-Coded Genetic Algorithm with SBX crossover ("ga"). leaf_cols str "all" "all", "path_used" Feature policy for leaf linear models. "all" fits over all features (with L1/L2 shrinkage); "path_used" restricts the leaf model strictly to features split along that leaf's ancestry path (winnowing). l1 float 0.0 [0.0, \infty) Lasso regularization penalty on leaf linear coefficients. Drives irrelevant leaf weights strictly to zero. l2 float 0.5 [0.0, \infty) Ridge regularization penalty on leaf linear coefficients. Stabilizes collinear inversion matrices in high-dimensional leaves. tau float 0.5 (0.0, 1.0) Quantile level when leaf="quantile". Optimizes asymmetric pinball loss for conditional quantile forecasting. tweedie_p float 1.5 [1.0, 2.0] Power parameter \(p\) for Tweedie exponential dispersion modeling. Ideal for zero-inflated insurance claims (\(1 < p < 2\)). tobit_threshold float 0.0 \(\mathbb{R}\) Censoring threshold \(y_c\) when leaf_family="tobit". Models left-censored Gaussian variables via expectation-maximization. leaf_digest bool True True, False Maintains streaming \(t\)-digests in leaves. Enables fast empirical prediction intervals (predict_interval(coverage=0.9)) without distributional assumptions. mars_degree int 1 [1, 3] Maximum interaction degree for MARS spline hinge functions within leaves. mars_terms int 10 [2, 50] Maximum number of basis terms retained in leaf spline models. mars_penalty float 2.0 [0.0, 10.0] Generalized cross-validation (GCV) penalty per knot for MARS leaf models.

items.title: 8. Growth and Leaf Controls
items.text:
Use the growth settings in sections 1–6 to configure the partition. Use the leaf settings in section 7 to configure the model fitted in each region. Under constraints, tree_monotone governs splits and leaf_monotone governs leaf coefficients. Supply data, feature names, types, and row weights to fit.

Parameter Type Default Description growth_control GrowthControl \| dict \| None None Groups split search, stopping, feature sampling, honesty, and pruning settings. leaf_control / control LeafControl \| dict \| None None Groups the leaf form, family, solver, penalties, and other leaf settings. train_groups bool True Whether to preserve grouped hierarchical entities during leaf retraining. train_ids bool False Whether to index training entity row keys in leaf sample caches (leaf_samples()).

For solver selection inside a leaf control, use solver="lbfgs" or another compatible solver. Flat callers can continue to use leaf_solver. Some leaf models use a dedicated fitting method. See the model reference for typed, dictionary, and flat examples.

Leaf model Compatible explicit solver choices Gaussian linear irls, lbfgs, ccd, shade, cmaes, ga, nes Linear binomial, probit, Poisson, Gamma, Tweedie, or Tobit irls, lbfgs Leaves with a dedicated estimator Use the estimator selected by the leaf form and family.

Use L-BFGS with zero L1 penalty and no monotone leaf constraints. It supports ridge penalties. Specialized estimators reject explicit solver selections.

items.title: 9. Telemetry & Execution Controls
items.text: Parameter Type Default Options Description verbose int 0 0, 1, 2, 3 Training verbosity. 0 = silent; 1 = live depth progress, per-depth summaries, and fit complete summary; 2 = stream per-node split candidates, winning features, threshold, gain, and leaf reasons; 3 = stream leaf solver optimization (GLM convergence iterations, deviance step, linear fit stats). seed int 42 int Deterministic random seed controlling feature subsampling (col_sample) and honest partition splits.

items.title: API reference — Evaluation reports
items.text: What Metrics returns, field by field — the contract every learner is scored under. Reports are plain dicts; missing pairs are dropped from the math and counted in n_missing, never hidden.

items.title: Metrics().regression(y_true, y_pred) → dict
items.text: field meaning n, n_missing observed pairs; dropped missing pairs mean_error mean(actual − fitted) — signed bias mean_pred / mean_true (1.0 = unbiased) mae, mad mean / median absolute deviation mape absolute % error, non-zero targets only rmse, r2, max_error the usual explained_variance 1 − Var(error)/Var(y) deciles per-target-decile error profile — the DAR "bathtub" view

items.title: Metrics().classification(y_true, y_pred, probabilities=None) → dict
items.text: field meaning n, n_missing, n_classes observed pairs; classes seen accuracy overall accuracy macro_precision/recall/f1 unweighted mean over classes per_class precision/recall/f1/support per class confusion counts matrix auc, logloss, brier only with probabilities (P(class 1))

items.title: Grouped reports
items.text:
classification_by_group(keys, ...) / regression_by_group(keys, y_true, y_pred) return one report per group, as a dict keyed by the group label — the format ModelTree's group API consumes.

Real values for every field on real data: the Metrics & plots showcase and the Metrics page example.

items.title: API reference — Anomaly & density trees
items.text: Unified anomaly detection: AnomalyModel (tree-based and PCA/NMF reconstruction errors), density estimation, streaming mass scoring, CoDisp, and contextual surprise.

items.title: AnomalyModel
items.text:
class AnomalyModel(kind: 'str' = 'eif', max_depth: 'int | None' = None, min_rows: 'int' = 10, contamination: 'float' = 0.05, seed: 'int' = 42, *, extension_level: 'int | None' = None, subsample_size: 'int | None' = None, min_samples_split: 'int | None' = None, alpha: 'float' = 0.0, min_density_gain: 'float' = 0.0, window_size: 'int' = 250, initial_mass: 'float' = 0.0, sample_size: 'int' = 256, eta: 'float' = 0.1, prior_weight: 'float' = 1.0, alphabet_size: 'int' = 256, smoothing_discount: 'float' = 0.5, **params: 'Any')

Unified Tree and Component-Based Anomaly Detector.

Wraps multiple tree-based and component reconstruction anomaly engines: - "eif" or "isolation": Extended Isolation Tree (oblique hyperplanes, mixed types). - "det" or "density": Density Estimation Tree (piecewise constant density, mixed types). - "hst" or "half_space": Streaming Half-Space Tree (mass-based scoring). - "rct" or "random_cut": Random Cut Tree (co-displacement scoring). - "active": Active Anomaly Tree with expert feedback adaptation. - "context": Variable-Order Context Anomaly Tree for discrete sequences. - "pca": Principal Component Analysis subspace reconstruction error. - "nmf": Non-negative Matrix Factorization additive reconstruction error.

items.title: Parameters
items.text: kind : str, default="eif" Anomaly tree engine to use: "eif", "det", "hst", "rct", "active", or "context". max_depth : int, optional Maximum tree depth. min_rows : int, default=10 Minimum leaf samples. contamination : float, default=0.05 Expected proportion of anomalies in the dataset (used to calibrate binary predictions). If the cutoff splits a group of equal scores, the entire group is labeled as inliers. seed : int, default=42 Random seed for stochastic engines (EIF, HST, RCT, Active). extension_level, subsample_size : int, optional EIF hyperplane order and training subsample size. min_samples_split : int, optional DET minimum samples per split. Defaults to twice min_rows. alpha, min_density_gain : float DET density smoothing and minimum gain. window_size : int, default=250 HST stream window size. initial_mass : float, default=0 HST initial node mass. sample_size : int, default=256 RCT sample size. eta, prior_weight : float Active anomaly learning rate and prior leaf weight. alphabet_size : int, default=256 Context tree alphabet size. smoothing_discount : float, default=0.5 Context tree discount for smoothing symbol probabilities.

items.title: API reference — Clustering trees
items.text: Unified clustering models and mixed-type search: ClusterModel, ClusterTree, TrieKNN, PCT (CLUS), CLTree, HDBSCAN Condensed Tree, and Unsupervised Random Forest (URF).

items.title: ClusterModel
items.text:
class ClusterModel(kind: 'str' = 'pct', n_clusters: 'int | None' = None, max_depth: 'int' = 6, min_rows: 'int' = 5, metric: 'str' = 'euclidean', seed: 'int' = 42, *, min_samples_split: 'int | None' = None, min_variance_reduction: 'float' = 0.0001, target_weights: 'Sequence[float] | None' = None, min_density: 'float' = 0.6, min_samples: 'int | None' = None, cluster_selection_epsilon: 'float' = 0.0, max_cluster_size: 'int | None' = None, cluster_selection_method: 'str' = 'eom', allow_single_cluster: 'bool' = False, n_trees: 'int' = 50, max_features: 'int | None' = None, linkage: 'str' = 'average', **params: 'Any')

Unified Tree-Based Clustering Model.

Wraps divisive and density-based tree clustering engines under a consistent API: - "pct" or "predictive": Predictive Clustering Trees (unsupervised or multi-target supervised, rules). - "cltree" or "density": CLTree (density-based spatial clustering tree with bounding boxes). - "hdbscan" or "hierarchical": HDBSCAN mutual reachability MST hierarchy. - "urf" or "proximity": Unsupervised Random Forest proximity-based clustering. - "pca": PCA component subspace clustering.

items.title: Parameters
items.text: kind : str, default="pct" Clustering engine: "pct", "cltree", "hdbscan", or "urf". n_clusters : int, optional Target cluster count (required for URF, auto-detected in HDBSCAN / CLTree). max_depth : int, default=6 Maximum tree depth for divisive clustering trees. min_rows : int, default=5 Minimum leaf samples / cluster size. metric : str, default="euclidean" Distance metric (for HDBSCAN: "euclidean", "manhattan", "chebyshev"). seed : int, default=42 Random seed for stochastic clustering algorithms (URF). min_samples_split : int, optional PCT minimum samples per split. Defaults to twice min_rows. min_variance_reduction : float, default=1e-4 PCT minimum reduction in target variance. target_weights : sequence of float, optional Per-target weights for PCT. min_density : float, default=0.6 CLTree minimum cluster density. min_samples : int, optional HDBSCAN neighbor count for core distances. Defaults to min_rows. cluster_selection_epsilon : float, default=0 HDBSCAN distance threshold for merging clusters. max_cluster_size : int, optional HDBSCAN upper limit on cluster size. cluster_selection_method : str, default="eom" HDBSCAN cluster selection method, "eom" or "leaf". allow_single_cluster : bool, default=False Allow HDBSCAN to select a single cluster. n_trees : int, default=50 Number of trees in the URF proximity forest. max_features : int, optional Number of URF features to consider per split. linkage : str, default="average" URF linkage method, "average", "single", or "complete".

items.title: API reference — Component & Factor Analysis
items.text: Consolidated component analysis: PCA with R-aligned factor rotations (Varimax, Quartimax, Promax), Truncated SVD, Whitening (ZCA/PCA), FastICA, and Non-negative Matrix Factorization (MU, ALS, HALS with L1/L2 penalties).

items.title: ComponentModel
items.text:
class ComponentModel(kind: 'str' = 'pca', n_components: 'int | None' = None, *, standardize: 'bool' = True, max_iter: 'int' = 200, tol: 'float' = 0.0001, seed: 'int' = 42, whitening_kind: 'str' = 'zca', eps: 'float' = 1e-05, rotation: 'str' = 'none', promax_m: 'float' = 4.0, solver: 'str' = 'hals', l1_reg: 'float' = 0.0, l2_reg: 'float' = 0.0) -> 'None'

Consolidated Component Analysis, Factor Analysis, and Dimensionality Reduction Model.

Provides a unified facade across multiple decomposition and factorization methods: - "pca": Classical Principal Component Analysis (centered and standardized). - "svd" or "truncated_svd": Truncated SVD without centering. - "whitening": ZCA and PCA covariance decorrelation preserving Mahalanobis geometry. - "ica" or "fastica": Independent Component Analysis via FastICA (negentropy/logcosh). - "nmf": Non-negative Matrix Factorization (MU, projected ALS, HALS coordinate descent with L1/L2 penalties). - "fa" or "factor_analysis": Exploratory Factor Analysis via Principal Axis Factoring (PAF / Minres), estimating shared communalities h^2 and uniquenesses psi = 1 - h^2 with Bartlett/Thomson scoring and Schmid-Leiman hierarchical bifactor decomposition.

items.title: Parameters
items.text: kind : str, default="pca" Decomposition engine: "pca", "svd", "whitening", "ica", "nmf", or "fa". n_components : int, optional Number of components or factors to extract. Defaults to min(n_samples, n_features). standardize : bool, default=True For PCA and Factor Analysis: center and scale columns to zero mean and unit variance. max_iter : int, default=200 Maximum iterations for iterative algorithms (ICA, NMF, FA). tol : float, default=1e-4 Convergence tolerance for iterative algorithms. seed : int, default=42 Random seed for stochastic initialization. whitening_kind : str, default="zca" For whitening: "zca" (zero-phase, minimal distortion) or "pca" whitening. eps : float, default=1e-5 Ridge regularization term added to eigenvalues in whitening. rotation : str, default="none" Factor/PCA rotation method aligned with R stats: - "none": Standard unrotated orthogonal eigenvectors. - "varimax": Orthogonal Varimax (gamma=1.0, R stats::varimax default). - "quartimax": Orthogonal Quartimax (gamma=0.0). - "equamax": Orthogonal Equamax (gamma=k/2). - "parsimax": Orthogonal Parsimax. - "biquartimax": Orthogonal Biquartimax (gamma=0.5). - "promax": Oblique Promax Procrustes rotation (R stats::promax). promax_m : float, default=4.0 Promax target exponent (default 4.0 in R stats::promax). solver : str, default="hals" Solver engine for NMF or Factor Analysis: - For NMF: "hals" (Hierarchical ALS), "als" (Projected ALS), "mu" (Multiplicative Updates). - For FA: "paf" (Principal Axis Factoring / Minres). l1_reg : float, default=0.0 L1 sparsity penalty for NMF HALS. l2_reg : float, default=0.0 L2 ridge penalty for NMF HALS/ALS.

items.title: API reference — Data
items.text: Typed ingest, the synthetic generator, dataset helpers and column screening. Guide with real examples: Data.

items.title: generate
items.text:
generate(n_rows=10000, n_numeric=5, cardinalities=None, hierarchy_levels=3, branching=None, group_effect_strength=0.5, hierarchy_effect_strength=0.3, interaction_strength=0.2, noise=0.1, task='regression', n_classes=2, tail_behavior='gaussian', missingness=0.0, seed=42)

Generate an adjustable benchmark dataset with known ground truth.

The knobs control how much signal lives in numeric effects, categorical levels, hierarchical groups and their interaction — so learners can be scored on structure recovery, not just accuracy. Deterministic for a given seed.

Args: n_rows: number of rows to generate. n_numeric: numeric feature columns; the first two carry linear signal. cardinalities: level count per categorical column (each >= 2). hierarchy_levels: depth of the categorical hierarchy (0 = none). branching: child count per hierarchy level (last value repeats). group_effect_strength: scale of categorical level effects. hierarchy_effect_strength: scale of hierarchy node effects. interaction_strength: scale of the numeric x categorical interaction. noise: scale of the residual noise. task: "regression" or "classification". n_classes: class count for classification (equal-frequency cuts). tail_behavior: "gaussian", "heavy" (Student-t residuals) or "bathtub" (noise grows with the signal — the DAR motivation). missingness: fraction of feature cells set to missing, in [0, 1). seed: RNG seed.

Returns: dict with columns (name -> values, None = missing), target, labels (classification only) and truth — the true effects plus truth["variance"], the realized variance share of each component.

Raises: ValueError: invalid parameter combination.

items.title: load_dataset
items.text:
load_dataset(name: 'str', auto_download: 'bool' = True) -> 'dict'

Load one dataset as name/columns/dtypes/n_rows/n_cols.

columns maps column name to a list with None for missing values; dtypes is "numeric" or "categorical" (strings/dictionaries).

items.title: list_datasets
items.text:
list_datasets() -> 'list[str]'

Names of currently available local datasets (parquet stems in repo or cache).

items.title: summarize
items.text:
summarize(values)

Summary of observed values, with missing counts shown by default.

NAs and NaNs are excluded from the statistics but always reported in n_missing — nothing is silently hidden.

Args: values: numeric values (None/NaN = missing).

Returns: dict with count (observed), n_missing, sum, mean, std, min, q1, median, q3, max (NaN for the statistics of an all-missing input).

items.title: winnow
items.text:
winnow(x, y, w=None, min_relevance=0.05)

Winnowing: screen columns by univariate relevance against the target and keep the relevant ones (the cheap pre-split screening LightGBM's docs call feature pre-filtering / winnowing).

Args: x: rows of predictors; None entries are missing. y: targets (rows with None targets or zero weight are dropped). w: optional row weights. min_relevance: keep columns with relevance >= this (default 0.05).

Returns: {"kept": [column indices], "relevance": [score per column]}.

items.title: DatasetBuilder
items.text:
class DatasetBuilder(n_category=None, na_policy='allow', digits=None, add_intercept=False)

Ingest any data into the typed dataset.

Owns the ingestion semantics: n_category category inference, explicit NA policy, digit rounding and an optional intercept column. Missing is None or NaN — both are counted in na_counts, and filling is opt-in only.

Args (constructor): n_category: integral numeric columns with at most this many distinct levels become categorical; values < 1 mean a fraction of rows (None = no inference). na_policy: "allow" (keep missing), "drop" (drop rows containing any missing) or "impute" (numeric mean, categorical mode). digits: round floats to this many decimal places (None = no rounding). add_intercept: append a constant 1.0 column named intercept.

items.title: DatasetBuilder.add_categorical
items.text:
add_categorical(self, /, name, values)

Add a categorical column from strings; the vocabulary is first-seen order. None = missing.

Args: name: column name. values: one level per row (None = missing).

items.title: DatasetBuilder.add_numeric
items.text:
add_numeric(self, /, name, values)

Add a numeric column. NaN is treated as missing.

Args: name: column name. values: one value per row (None/NaN = missing).

items.title: DatasetBuilder.build
items.text:
build(self, /)

Build the typed dataset with the configured policies applied.

Returns: dict with columns (name -> values), dtypes ("numeric" or "categorical"), na_counts (missing per column), n_rows, n_cols.

Raises: ValueError: inconsistent column lengths, duplicate names, invalid policy usage (e.g. "drop" removing every row).

items.title: API reference — Encoders & scalers
items.text: Pipeline tools for feeding downstream algorithms (sklearn and friends) — never invoked by the tree. Guide: Data.

items.title: IndexMapper
items.text:
class IndexMapper()

Categorical string <-> stable code mapping (sklearn-style fit/transform).

items.title: IndexMapper.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, name, values)

Learn the vocabulary of name (first-seen order). Re-fitting resets it.

items.title: IndexMapper.get_all_names
items.text:
get_all_names(self, /, name)

All fitted levels in code order.

Raises: ValueError: column not fitted.

items.title: IndexMapper.get_index
items.text:
get_index(self, /, name, value)

Code for one level (None when the level is unseen).

Raises: ValueError: column not fitted.

items.title: IndexMapper.get_name
items.text:
get_name(self, /, name, index)

Level for one code.

Raises: ValueError: column not fitted or code out of range.

items.title: IndexMapper.inverse_transform
items.text:
inverse_transform(self, /, name, codes)

Map codes back to their string levels.

Args: name: fitted column name. codes: codes per row (None = missing).

Returns: string levels (None where the code is missing).

Raises: ValueError: column not fitted or code out of range.

items.title: IndexMapper.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, name, values)

Codes for values; unseen levels map to None (missing).

items.title: VariableScaler
items.text:
class VariableScaler()

Per-column distributional scaling — each variable transformed independently (legacy VariableTransformation semantics).

Same strategy names as GroupedScaler, applied per column, with exact inverse_transform. None/NaN are missing and pass through as missing; degenerate scales give missing, never inf.

items.title: VariableScaler.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, columns, strategy)

Fit all columns at once under the given strategy.

Args: columns: {name: values} for every column to scale (None/NaN = missing; counted in each column's n_missing). strategy: strategy name (see GroupedScaler).

Raises: ValueError: unknown strategy.

items.title: VariableScaler.inverse_transform
items.text:
inverse_transform(self, /, name, values)

Exact inverse of transform under the fitted statistics.

Args: name: fitted column name. values: previously transformed values.

Returns: original-scale values (up to floating-point error).

Raises: ValueError: not fitted or unknown column.

items.title: VariableScaler.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, name, values)

Scale one fitted column's values.

Args: name: fitted column name. values: numeric values (None/NaN = missing).

Returns: scaled values; None for missing inputs and degenerate scales.

Raises: ValueError: not fitted or unknown column.

items.title: GroupedScaler
items.text:
class GroupedScaler()

Fit/transform group distributional scaling with exact inverse (sklearn-shaped: fit once, then transform / inverse_transform).

Strategies: centered family — "zscore", "min-max", "median-iqr", "mean-iqr", "median-qd", "median-std", "median-range", "mean-range", "min-qd", "min-iqr"; ratio family — "min", "max", "mean", "median", "iqr", "qd", "std", "range". Missing in -> missing out; degenerate (zero) scales give missing, never inf.

items.title: GroupedScaler.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, keys, values, strategy)

Fit group statistics of values under the given strategy.

Args: keys: group label per row (None = missing). values: numeric value per row (None/NaN = missing; counted in each group's n_missing). strategy: strategy name (see the class docstring).

Raises: ValueError: unknown strategy or mismatched lengths.

items.title: GroupedScaler.inverse_transform
items.text:
inverse_transform(self, /, keys, values)

Exact inverse of transform under the fitted statistics.

Args: keys: group label per row. values: previously transformed values.

Returns: original-scale values (up to floating-point error).

Raises: ValueError: not fitted or mismatched lengths.

items.title: GroupedScaler.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, keys, values)

Scale values against the fitted group statistics.

Args: keys: group label per row. values: numeric value per row.

Returns: scaled values; None for missing key/value, unseen groups and degenerate scales.

Raises: ValueError: not fitted or mismatched lengths.

items.title: BaseNEncoder
items.text:
class BaseNEncoder(base)

Base-N / binary encoding: each level becomes its base-base digits as indicator columns (base = 2 is the classic Binary encoder). Task: both (unsupervised). Unseen and missing rows are all-zero.

items.title: BaseNEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values)

Fit the level vocabulary on values.

items.title: BaseNEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Returns {digit name: indicator list}.

items.title: CatBoostEncoder
items.text:
class CatBoostEncoder(prior, permutations, seed)

CatBoost-style ordered target statistics — the leakage-safe flavour.

fit_transform gives each row the running statistic of its level using only rows earlier in a shuffled order: (sum_y_prefix + prior * global) / (n_prefix + 1), averaged over permutations seeded passes. The same level gets different values in different rows — that row-dependence is the anti-leakage mechanism. transform (new data) uses prior-smoothed fitted level means.

items.title: CatBoostEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y)

Fit prior-smoothed level means (used by transform on new data).

items.title: CatBoostEncoder.fit_transform
items.text:
fit_transform(self, /, values, y)

Leakage-safe ordered encodings of the training rows themselves.

items.title: CatBoostEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Encode new rows from the fitted level means; unseen -> global mean, missing -> None.

items.title: CountEncoder
items.text:
class CountEncoder(normalize)

Count / frequency encoding: occurrence count per category (normalize gives the share of rows). Task: both (unsupervised). Unseen levels give 0.0; missing stays missing.

items.title: CountEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values)

Fit counts on values.

items.title: CountEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Count (or share) per row; unseen -> 0.0, missing -> None.

items.title: EmbeddingEncoder
items.text:
class EmbeddingEncoder(dim, lr, epochs, seed, task)

NN-style learned embeddings per category: a small embedding table and a linear head trained by SGD, one table per categorical feature. Task: both — softmax head for classification; for regression a ReLU output when all fitted targets are non-negative, linear otherwise. transform returns the embeddings, predict the trained head. Unseen levels give zeros; missing stays missing.

items.title: EmbeddingEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y, n_classes=None)

Train on (values, y); n_classes is inferred for classification when omitted, ignored for regression.

items.title: EmbeddingEncoder.predict
items.text:
predict(self, /, values)

Predictions of the trained head (class label or activated value).

items.title: EmbeddingEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Learned embedding per row (None = missing, zeros = unseen).

items.title: HashingEncoder
items.text:
class HashingEncoder(n_buckets)

Hashed one-hot: levels are hashed into n_buckets indicator columns, so unseen levels still land somewhere. Deterministic.

items.title: HashingEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Returns {bucket name: indicator list}.

items.title: JamesSteinEncoder
items.text:
class JamesSteinEncoder()

James-Stein encoding: level means shrunk toward the grand mean with B = max(0, 1 - ((L - 3) * sigma2) / sum((mean_i - global)^2)); fewer than three levels collapse to the grand mean. Task: both. Unseen -> global; missing -> None.

items.title: JamesSteinEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y)

Fit shrunk means on (values, y).

items.title: JamesSteinEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Shrunk mean per row; unseen -> global, missing -> None.

items.title: LeaveOneOutEncoder
items.text:
class LeaveOneOutEncoder()

Leave-one-out encoding: fit_transform gives each row its level's mean target without that row (leakage-aware); transform on new data uses the full fitted level mean. Task: both. Unseen -> global mean; missing -> None.

items.title: LeaveOneOutEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y)

Fit level means on (values, y).

items.title: LeaveOneOutEncoder.fit_transform
items.text:
fit_transform(self, /, values, y)

Row-level means excluding each row's own target.

items.title: LeaveOneOutEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Full fitted level means for new rows.

items.title: MEstimatorEncoder
items.text:
class MEstimatorEncoder(m)

M-estimate encoding: (sum_y + m * global) / (n_level + m) — target smoothing with fixed strength m. Task: both (leaky on training data; prefer CatBoostEncoder or LeaveOneOutEncoder there). Unseen -> global; missing -> None.

items.title: MEstimatorEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y)

Fit smoothed level means on (values, y).

items.title: MEstimatorEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Smoothed mean per row; unseen -> global, missing -> None.

items.title: OneHotEncoder
items.text:
class OneHotEncoder()

One-hot expansion: one indicator column per fitted level (first-seen order). Missing values and levels unseen at fit produce an all-zero row.

items.title: OneHotEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values)

Learn the levels (first-seen order). Re-fitting resets them.

items.title: OneHotEncoder.levels
items.text:
levels(self, /)

Fitted levels, in column order.

items.title: OneHotEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Returns {level: indicator list}; unseen/missing rows are all-zero.

items.title: QuantileEncoder
items.text:
class QuantileEncoder(q, smoothing)

Quantile encoding: each level becomes its smoothed target quantile (default median), w * level_quantile + (1 - w) * global_quantile with w = n / (n + smoothing). Task: regression. Unseen -> global quantile; missing -> None.

items.title: QuantileEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y)

Fit quantiles on (values, y).

items.title: QuantileEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Smoothed quantile per row; unseen -> global, missing -> None.

items.title: SumEncoder
items.text:
class SumEncoder()

Sum contrast coding: k-1 columns; level i < k-1 gets +1 in column i, the last level gets -1 across all columns. Task: both (unsupervised). Unseen rows give zeros; missing stays missing.

items.title: SumEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values)

Fit the level vocabulary on values.

items.title: SumEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Contrast row per row (None = missing).

items.title: TargetEncoder
items.text:
class TargetEncoder(smoothing)

Smoothed target encoding (fitted-mean flavour).

w * level_mean + (1 - w) * global_mean with w = n / (n + smoothing). Leaky on training data (the row's own target is in its level mean) — prefer CatBoostEncoder.fit_transform for training features. Unseen levels fall back to the global mean; missing stays missing.

items.title: TargetEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y)

Fit level means on (values, y).

items.title: TargetEncoder.prior
items.text:
prior(self, /)

The global mean used as the unseen-level fallback.

items.title: TargetEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

Encode values; unseen -> global mean, missing -> None.

items.title: TfidfEncoder
items.text:
class TfidfEncoder(normalize)

Class-level TF-IDF: each category becomes a vector over the target classes — tf(v,j) = count(v,j)/count(v) times idf(j) = ln(1 + n/(1 + count(j))) + 1; normalize scales each level vector to unit L2 norm. Task: classification. Unseen levels fall back to the global class shares; missing stays missing.

items.title: TfidfEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y, n_classes)

Fit class counts on (values, y, n_classes).

items.title: TfidfEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

One class-space vector per row (None = missing).

items.title: WoEEncoder
items.text:
class WoEEncoder(prior)

Weight of Evidence (credit-risk classic): one-vs-rest ln(distr_j(v) / distr_not_j(v)) per category, smoothed with additive prior. Task: classification. Positive = over-representation of the class in that level. Unseen levels give neutral zeros; missing stays missing.

items.title: WoEEncoder.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, values, y, n_classes)

Fit class counts on (values, y, n_classes).

items.title: WoEEncoder.transform
items.text:
transform(self, /, values)

One WoE vector per row (None = missing).

items.title: API reference — Feature functions
items.text: Grouped/trended/windowed transforms, lags and calendar parts. Guide: Data processing.

items.title: grouped_scale
items.text:
grouped_scale(keys, values, strategy='zscore')

One-shot group scaling: fit on (keys, values) and transform the same rows.

Each row's value is scaled by its group's summary under strategy (centered family like "zscore" or ratio family like "mean"; see GroupedScaler for the full list and the exact inverse).

Args: keys: group label per row (None = missing). values: numeric value per row (None/NaN = missing). strategy: one of "zscore", "min-max", "median-iqr", "mean-iqr", "median-qd", "median-std", "median-range", "mean-range", "min-qd", "min-iqr", "min", "max", "mean", "median", "iqr", "qd", "std", "range".

Returns: scaled values; rows with a missing key/value, an unseen group or a degenerate (zero) scale give None — missing in, missing out.

Raises: ValueError: unknown strategy or mismatched lengths.

items.title: grouped_transform
items.text:
grouped_transform(keys, values, kind='mean')

Per-row group summary of values within groups defined by keys.

Args: keys: group label per row (None = missing). values: numeric value per row (None/NaN = missing; excluded from the group statistics but counted in each group's n_missing). kind: "mean", "sum", "std", "count", "min", "max", "median", "q1" or "q3".

Returns: the summary of each row's group; rows with a missing key/value or an unseen group give None.

Raises: ValueError: unknown kind or mismatched lengths.

items.title: trended_transform
items.text:
trended_transform(keys, dates, values, granularity='year_month', kind='mean', hemisphere='north')

Grouped summary trended at a time granularity.

Each row gets the summary of its (key x time-bucket) cell — e.g. with granularity "year_month" and kind "mean", the row's key-and-month mean. Incomplete rows (missing key/date/value) are dropped from estimation and reported via a warning.

Args: keys: series label per row (None = missing). dates: ISO date strings per row (None = missing). values: numeric values per row (None/NaN = missing). granularity: bucket spec joined by "_" from {year, halfyear, season, quarter, month, week, weekday, day} — e.g. "year_month", "year_week", "month_weekday". kind: summary kind ("mean", "sum", "std", "count", "min", "max", "median", "q1", "q3"). hemisphere: "north" or "south" (affects the season component).

Returns: per-row cell summaries; incomplete rows give None.

Raises: ValueError: unknown granularity/kind/hemisphere, unparseable date or mismatched lengths.

items.title: windowed_transform
items.text:
windowed_transform(keys, dates, values, window_days=7, kind='mean', include_current=True)

Trailing-window aggregation per key over day windows.

Each row summarizes the observed values of its key in a window of window_days days; incomplete rows (missing key/date/value) are dropped from estimation and reported via a warning.

Args: keys: series label per row (None = missing). dates: ISO date strings per row (None = missing). values: numeric values per row (None/NaN = missing). window_days: window length in days (>= 1); covering the window_days days ending at the row's date, or strictly earlier days when include_current is false. kind: summary kind ("mean", "sum", "std", "count", "min", "max", "median", "q1", "q3"). include_current: include the row's own date in the window.

Returns: per-row window summaries; None for incomplete rows and for empty/all-missing windows.

Raises: ValueError: window_days == 0, unknown kind, unparseable date or mismatched lengths.

items.title: lag_by_days
items.text:
lag_by_days(keys, dates, values, lag_days)

Lag values by whole days within each key (day granularity).

Each row receives the value of its key at date - lag_days; duplicate (key, date) rows keep the last occurrence. Incomplete rows (missing key/date/value) are dropped from estimation and reported via a warning.

Args: keys: series label per row (None = missing). dates: ISO date strings per row (None = missing). values: numeric values per row (None/NaN = missing). lag_days: lag in whole days (0 returns the row's own value).

Returns: lagged values; None where no source row exists.

Raises: ValueError: unparseable date or mismatched lengths.

items.title: decomposed_transform
items.text:
decomposed_transform(keys, dates, values, season_granularity='month', trend_window=3, hemisphere='north')

Additive decomposition, following the statsmodels seasonal_decompose (additive) convention.

The trend is a centered moving average over each key's rows ordered by date; the seasonal component is the mean of (series - trend) per (key, season bucket), estimated from rows with a complete trend window. Incomplete rows (missing key/date/value) are dropped from estimation and reported via a warning.

Args: keys: series label per row (None = missing). dates: ISO date strings per row (None = missing). values: numeric values per row (None/NaN = missing). season_granularity: bucket spec for the seasonal component (e.g. "month", "weekday" — same vocabulary as trended_transform). trend_window: centered moving-average window in rows (>= 1). hemisphere: "north" or "south" (affects the season component).

Returns: dict with detrended (series - trend), deseasonalized (series - seasonal) and residual (series - trend - seasonal); incomplete rows give None.

Raises: ValueError: trend_window == 0, unknown granularity/hemisphere, unparseable date or mismatched lengths.

items.title: calendar_features
items.text:
calendar_features(dates, hemisphere='north')

Calendar features for ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD or timestamp prefix).

Produces year, halfyear, quarter, month, week (ISO), iso_year, weekday (0 = Monday), day, day_of_year, season and weekend as numeric parts, ready for tree learners.

Args: dates: ISO date strings or timestamps (None = missing). hemisphere: "north" or "south" (southern shifts the season by six months).

Returns: dict of 11 feature lists aligned with dates; rows with a missing date give None features.

Raises: ValueError: unparseable date or unknown hemisphere.

items.title: API reference — Metrics
items.text: Complete evaluation reports at once. Guides: Metrics, Evaluation reports.

items.title: Metrics
items.text:
class Metrics()

One metrics class computing complete reports at once — the yardstick every learner is measured with. Task: both. Pairs with a missing/NaN side are dropped from the math and reported in n_missing, never hidden.

items.title: Metrics.brier_score
items.text:
brier_score(self, /, y_true, probs)

Brier score of probability predictions. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). probs: predicted probabilities.

Returns: mean squared probability error.

items.title: Metrics.calibration
items.text:
calibration(self, /, y_true, scores, n_bins=10)

Calibration (reliability) bins: mean predicted score vs observed frequency per bin. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). scores: predicted scores/probabilities. n_bins: equal-width bins over [0, 1] (default 10).

Returns: {"bins": [{"left", "right", "mean_score", "observed", "n"}]} (empty bins omitted; scores clip into edge bins).

items.title: Metrics.classification
items.text:
classification(self, /, y_true, y_pred, probabilities=None)

Complete classification report: accuracy, macro averages, per-class precision/recall/f1/support, confusion matrix — and with probabilities (P(class 1)) also logloss, brier and ROC-AUC.

Args: y_true: integer class labels (None/NaN = missing). y_pred: predicted labels (None/NaN = missing). probabilities: P(class 1) per row; enables the probabilistic metrics.

Returns: the full report as a dict.

Raises: ValueError: mismatched lengths, non-integer labels or no observed pairs.

items.title: Metrics.classification_by_group
items.text:
classification_by_group(self, /, keys, y_true, y_pred)

Classification report per group key (sorted by key). Task: classification.

Args: keys: group label per row (rows with missing key/labels skip). y_true: integer class labels. y_pred: integer class labels.

Returns: {group: classification_report}.

items.title: Metrics.classification_scores
items.text:
classification_scores(self, /, y_true, y_pred)

Single-label classification scorecard (binary or multiclass). Task: classification.

Args: y_true: integer-like labels. y_pred: integer-like labels.

Returns: {"n", "n_classes", "accuracy", "balanced_accuracy", "precision_macro/micro/weighted", "recall_*", "f1_*", "mcc", "jaccard_macro/micro/weighted", "hamming_loss", "zero_one_loss"}.

items.title: Metrics.competing_risks
items.text:
competing_risks(self, /, durations, events, cif_curves=None, risk_scores=None, times=None)

Complete competing risks report for multi-cause survival endpoints: cause-specific Harrell's C, Uno's IPCW C, cause-specific IBS and time-dependent Brier scores over specified or sample decile evaluation horizons.

Args: durations: observed follow-up times. events: event indicators (0 = censored, 1..J = mutually exclusive causes). cif_curves: optional CIF curves mapping {cause: (N, T)} or 3D list (N, n_causes, T). risk_scores: optional risk scores mapping {cause: (N,)} or 2D list (N, n_causes). times: optional evaluation horizon times grid.

items.title: Metrics.competing_risks_calibration
items.text:
competing_risks_calibration(self, /, durations, events, predicted_cif, horizon)

Competing risks calibration report across causes (Alberge et al. 2026).

items.title: Metrics.d_calibration
items.text:
d_calibration(self, /, durations, events, surv_at_durations, n_bins=10)

D-Calibration test (Haider et al. 2020) for survival distribution uniformity.

items.title: Metrics.decile_table
items.text:
decile_table(self, /, y_true, scores, n_buckets=10)

Decile profile (kds/PerfScoreCard decile table; modelplotpy response at decile granularity). Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). scores: predicted scores/probabilities. n_buckets: equal-count buckets by score descending (default 10).

Returns: [{"decile", "n", "avg_score", "events", "event_rate", "cum_capture", "cum_event_rate", "lift"}, ...] (decile 1 = top).

items.title: Metrics.double_lift
items.text:
double_lift(self, /, y_true, scores_a, scores_b, n_buckets=10)

Double-lift table: actual vs model A vs model B along A's ranking (CAS monograph chart; additive vs ratio display is a plotting concern). Task: regression or classification.

Args: y_true: targets. scores_a: model A predictions (defines the ranking). scores_b: model B predictions. n_buckets: equal-count buckets (default 10).

Returns: [{"bucket", "n", "actual", "pred_a", "pred_b"}, ...].

items.title: Metrics.gain_curve
items.text:
gain_curve(self, /, y_true, scores)

Cumulative gains curve. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). scores: predicted scores/probabilities.

Returns: {"points": [[population_fraction, capture_rate], ...]} (lift at a point = capture / fraction).

items.title: Metrics.hinge_loss
items.text:
hinge_loss(self, /, y_true, decision)

Hinge loss over signed decision margins. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). decision: decision-function margins (signed).

Returns: mean hinge loss.

items.title: Metrics.lift_curve
items.text:
lift_curve(self, /, y_true, scores)

Cumulative lift curve. Task: classification.

Multilabel scorecard: rows are instances, columns are labels, entries

0.5 are positive (raw entries double as ranking scores). Task: multilabel classification.

Args: y_true: label matrix (rows x labels, 0/1). y_scores: prediction/score matrix (same shape).

items.text:

Pairwise distances between two row sets. Task: any.

Args: a: first rows (rows x features). b: second rows (same width). metric: "euclidean" | "manhattan" | "chebyshev" | "minkowski" | "cosine" | "correlation" | "hamming" | "jaccard". p: Minkowski power (default 2.0).

items.title: Metrics.pr_curve
items.text:
pr_curve(self, /, y_true, scores)

items.title: Metrics.regression
items.text:
regression(self, /, y_true, y_pred)

Complete regression report: n, n_missing, mean_error (actual - fitted), bias (mean_pred / mean_true), mae, mad, mape (non-zero targets), rmse, r2, max_error, explained_variance and deciles — the DAR per-target-decile error profile (the bathtub view).

Args: y_true: actual values (None/NaN = missing). y_pred: fitted values (None/NaN = missing).

Returns: the full report as a dict.

Raises: ValueError: mismatched lengths or no observed pairs.

items.title: Metrics.regression_by_group
items.text:
regression_by_group(self, /, keys, y_true, y_pred)

Regression report per group (keys: dates, categories, ...) — the legacy per-key summary lineage. Rows with a missing key are ignored.

Args: keys: group label per row (None = ignored). y_true: actual values (None/NaN = missing). y_pred: fitted values (None/NaN = missing).

Returns: {group: regression report}, sorted by group.

Raises: ValueError: mismatched lengths or a group with no observed pairs.

items.title: Metrics.roc_curve
items.text:

items.text:
stability_index(self, /, reference, current, n_bins=10)

Stability index (PSI on scores, CSI on a feature column). Task: classification or regression monitoring.

Args: reference: reference-period values (bins derive from their range). current: current-period values. n_bins: equal-width bins (default 10).

Returns: {"psi": float, "bins": [{"left", "right", "reference_share", "current_share", "contribution"}, ...]}.

items.title: Metrics.survival
items.text:
survival(self, /, durations, events, risk_scores, surv_curves=None, times=None)

Complete survival analysis report (Harrell C-index, Uno IPCW C-index, Integrated Brier Score).

Args: durations: observed duration / time-to-event per row. events: event indicator (1.0 = event observed, 0.0 = right-censored). risk_scores: predicted risk score (higher score = shorter expected survival). surv_curves: optional individual survival probability curves S(t|x) matrix (N, K). times: optional evaluation horizon times grid.

items.title: Metrics.time_series
items.text:
time_series(self, /, y_true, y_pred, y_train=None, seasonal_period=None, std_pred=None)

Complete time series forecasting report (MAE, RMSE, MASE, sMAPE, WAPE, MDA, CRPS).

Args: y_true: actual time series targets. y_pred: predicted values. y_train: optional in-sample training series (used to scale MASE). seasonal_period: optional seasonality m (e.g. 7 for daily, 12 for monthly). std_pred: optional predicted standard deviation per period (used for Gaussian CRPS).

items.title: Metrics.uplift
items.text:
uplift(self, /, y_true, treatment, tau_pred)

Complete causal uplift and Qini curve report.

Args: y_true: observed outcome per row. treatment: binary treatment indicator (1.0 = treated, 0.0 = control). tau_pred: predicted treatment effect / uplift score per row.

Returns: dict with ATE, Qini coefficient, normalized Qini, AUUC, decile uplifts, Qini curve.

items.title: Metrics.weighted_kappa

weighted_kappa(self, /, y_true, y_pred, weights='quadratic')

Cohen's kappa with optional weights over the label scale. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: integer-like labels. y_pred: integer-like labels. weights: "none" | "linear" | "quadratic" (default "quadratic").

Returns: kappa (1 = perfect agreement).

items.title: API reference — ModelTree
items.text: The model tree: typed fit, split-search knobs, quantiles, training log. Guide: Model.

items.title: ModelTree
items.text:
class ModelTree(*args, growth_control=None, leaf_control=None, **kwargs)

Model tree: greedy splits with Gaussian, binomial-logit or Poisson-log leaves, NA-aware (learned split directions + NA-indicator leaf terms). Task: regression, binary probability estimation, or count modeling.

items.title: ModelTree.apply
items.text:
apply(self, /, x)

Return the leaf ID (0..n_leaves-1) for each input row.

Args: x: raw rows of predictors.

Returns: one integer leaf ID per row.

items.title: ModelTree.break_down
items.text:
break_down(self, /, row)

DALEX-style break-down of one response-scale prediction.

Args: row: one row of predictors (None = missing). Accepts mixed numeric and categorical strings.

Returns: {"baseline", "steps": [[column_name, contribution], ...], "residual", "prediction"}; baseline + steps + residual == prediction.

items.title: ModelTree.cdf
items.text:
cdf(self, /, x, value)

Fitted binomial/Poisson CDF P(Y <= value), conditional on each row.

Args: x: raw rows of predictors, with the same missing/level handling as predict. value: response threshold; discrete CDFs use its integer floor.

Returns: one fitted-distribution probability per row. Unlike quantile, this uses the fitted family, not the empirical target t-digest.

Raises: ValueError for Gaussian leaves or an invalid threshold.

items.title: ModelTree.fit
items.text:
fit(self, /, x, y, w=None, dtypes=None, control=None, id_col=None, group_col=None, col_names=None, event=None, treatment=None, n_classes=None, sample_weight=None, row_weights=None, col_weights=None, feature_weights=None, train_groups=None, train_ids=None, fairness_penalty=None, protected_col=None, protected_attribute=None, fairness_metric=None, sporf_d=None, sporf_projections=None, extratrees=None, ebm_fast=None)

Fit the tree on row-major data using the selected leaf family.

Args: x: rows of predictors; None entries are missing (NA rows train). y: targets; None/NaN drops that row for binomial/Poisson. Gaussian NaN handling follows the historical Gaussian path. Binomial targets are 0 or 1; Poisson targets are finite nonnegative counts or rates (including fractional values). Gaussian targets retain ordinary regression. w: optional per-row sample weights (row weightage); zero-weight rows are ignored. dtypes: optional per-column types — "numeric" (default) or "categorical" (values are level codes; the split search partitions levels, no encoding).

Returns: nothing; the fitted tree replaces the inner model.

items.title: ModelTree.leaves
items.text:
leaves(self, /)

Fitted leaf models with their empirical target distribution stats.

Args: none.

Returns: one dict per leaf with cols, coef, na_coef, intercept, response_constant, n, mean, std, min, max, quantiles. Linear coef, na_coef, and intercept use the family's link scale (identity, logit, or log); mean and other stats describe raw targets. Constant leaves have no link-scale coefficient vector: intercept is None, while response_constant is the response-scale constant.

items.title: ModelTree.quantile
items.text:
quantile(self, /, x, tau)

Empirical conditional target quantiles from the leaves' t-digests: any tau in [0, 1] after fitting. These are not quantiles of the fitted binomial/Poisson distribution; use cdf for that distribution's CDF.

Args: x: rows of predictors (NA never blocks). tau: quantile level.

Returns: one quantile per row (NaN when a leaf's digest was dropped).

items.title: ModelTree.retrain
items.text:
retrain(self, /, x, y, control=None, w=None, mode='internal', leaf_features=None, retrain_cols=None, col_names=None, leaf=None, leaf_family=None, leaf_cols=None, l1=None, l2=None, leaf_digest=None, tau=None, event=None, n_classes=None)

Retrain all leaf models on new or existing data without altering tree topology or splits.

Args: x: rows of predictors; None entries are missing. y: targets. control: optional LeafControl instance or dict. w: optional sample weights. mode: "internal" (updates self in place and returns self) or "external" (returns new ModelTree clone). leaf_features: optional subset of column indices or names for leaf models. retrain_cols: alias for leaf_features. col_names: optional data column names to validate and remap splits. leaf: optional leaf kind override ("linear", "mean", "median", "quantile", "huber"). leaf_family: optional leaf distribution override ("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson"). leaf_cols: optional leaf columns policy override ("all", "path_used"). l1: optional lasso penalty override. l2: optional ridge penalty override. leaf_digest: optional bool whether to keep leaf t-digests. tau: optional quantile tau when leaf is "quantile" (default 0.5).

Returns: updated ModelTree (self for internal mode, or new ModelTree for external mode).

The Rust core owns the shared optimization seam. Python callers reach it through mltreelib.solvers.optimize. Guide: Generic optimizer.

Reach the module through mltreelib_core::generic or mltreelib_core::solver::generic. The short names Bounds, Budget, Constraint, ConstraintKind, Objective, ObjectiveError, OptimizationRequest, OptimizationResult, OptimizerKind, SmoothObjective, and SolveStatus are re-exported from mltreelib_core::solver.

A bound is either finite or infinite. lower[i] <= upper[i] holds for every dimension. A fully unbounded domain uses negative and positive infinity.

items.title: Budget
items.text:
pub struct Budget {

Counts user objective evaluations and solver iterations.

One counter covers every user objective call, including calls inside local solves, perturbation steps, population initialization, finite-difference gradients, and archive updates. The counters use interior mutability, so the objective wrapper and the solver share one budget without aliasing borrows.

items.title: fit
items.text:
fit(X, y, *, family='gaussian', solver='auto', l1=0.0, l2=0.0, sample_weight=None, monotone=None, max_iter=250, tol=1e-09, seed=42, tweedie_p=None, tobit_threshold=None)

Fits a weighted Gaussian or generalized linear model without growing a tree.

Pass one numeric design matrix and one response per row. Use nonnegative case weights with a positive total weight. The solver picks the exact Gaussian path when it fits the family and the requested penalties.

items.title: optimize
items.text:
optimize(objective, bounds, *, method='random_search', start=None, max_evaluations=None, max_iterations=None, tol=1e-06, seed=0, gradient=None, samples=None, initial_population=None, constraints=None, constraint_kind='inequality', local_method=None)

Minimizes a callable scalar objective inside bounds.

The objective receives one list of parameter values and returns one finite scalar. The optional gradient callable receives the same list and returns one value per parameter. Smooth methods use a central-difference fallback when no gradient is supplied. For COBYLA, constraints returns a fixed-length sequence of finite inequality residuals. Nonnegative residuals are feasible. For basin hopping, local_method selects the inner optimizer.
